title: षट्षष्टितमोऽध्यायः
titleEn: Adhyaya 66 · Duryodhana demands a second game

summary.en: Duryodhana, Karna and Shakuni persuade Dhritarashtra that the Pandavas, now enemies, must be ruined, and propose a second game in which the loser will spend twelve years in the forest and a thirteenth in hiding. Gandhari begs her husband to abandon Duryodhana, but Dhritarashtra recalls the Pandavas.
summary.kn: ಈಗ ಶತ್ರುಗಳಾದ ಪಾಂಡವರನ್ನು ನಾಶಮಾಡಲೇಬೇಕೆಂದು ದುರ್ಯೋಧನ, ಕರ್ಣ, ಶಕುನಿ ಧೃತರಾಷ್ಟ್ರನನ್ನು ಒಪ್ಪಿಸಿ, ಸೋತವರು ಹನ್ನೆರಡು ವರ್ಷ ವನವಾಸ, ಹದಿಮೂರನೆಯದು ಅಜ್ಞಾತವಾಸ ಮಾಡಬೇಕೆಂಬ ಎರಡನೆಯ ಜೂಜನ್ನು ಸೂಚಿಸುತ್ತಾರೆ. ದುರ್ಯೋಧನನನ್ನು ತ್ಯಜಿಸೆಂದು ಗಾಂಧಾರಿ ಬೇಡಿದರೂ ಧೃತರಾಷ್ಟ್ರನು ಪಾಂಡವರನ್ನು ಮರಳಿ ಕರೆಸುತ್ತಾನೆ.
summary.hi: दुर्योधन, कर्ण और शकुनि धृतराष्ट्र को समझाते हैं कि अब शत्रु बने पाण्डवों को नष्ट करना ही होगा, और दूसरे द्यूत का प्रस्ताव करते हैं जिसमें हारने वाला बारह वर्ष वन में और तेरहवाँ अज्ञातवास में बिताएगा। गान्धारी पति से दुर्योधन को त्यागने की विनती करती हैं, पर धृतराष्ट्र पाण्डवों को वापस बुलाते हैं।
summary.te: ఇప్పుడు శత్రువులైన పాండవులను నాశనం చేయాల్సిందేనని దుర్యోధనుడు, కర్ణుడు, శకుని ధృతరాష్ట్రుని ఒప్పించి, ఓడినవారు పన్నెండేళ్లు వనవాసం, పదమూడవది అజ్ఞాతవాసం చేయాలనే రెండవ జూదాన్ని సూచిస్తారు. దుర్యోధనుని విడిచిపెట్టమని గాంధారి వేడుకున్నా ధృతరాష్ట్రుడు పాండవులను తిరిగి పిలిపిస్తాడు.
summary.ta: இப்போது பகைவர்களான பாண்டவர்களை அழித்தே தீர வேண்டும் என்று துரியோதனன், கர்ணன், ஶகுனி திருதராஷ்டிரனை இணங்க வைத்து, தோற்றவர் பன்னிரண்டு ஆண்டு வனவாசமும் பதின்மூன்றாம் ஆண்டு அஜ்ஞாதவாசமும் செய்ய வேண்டும் என்ற இரண்டாம் சூதை முன்வைக்கிறார்கள். துரியோதனனைக் கைவிடுமாறு காந்தாரி கணவனை வேண்டியும் திருதராஷ்டிரன் பாண்டவர்களைத் திரும்ப அழைக்கிறான்.
summary.ml: പാണ്ഡവർ ഇപ്പോൾ ശത്രുക്കളാണെന്നും അവരെ നശിപ്പിക്കണമെന്നും ദുര്യോധനനും കർണ്ണനും ശകുനിയും ധൃതരാഷ്ട്രരെ ബോധ്യപ്പെടുത്തുന്നു; തോൽക്കുന്നവർ പന്ത്രണ്ടു വർഷം കാട്ടിലും പതിമൂന്നാമത്തേത് ഒളിവിലും കഴിയണമെന്ന രണ്ടാമത്തെ ചൂതുകളി നിർദേശിക്കുന്നു. ദുര്യോധനനെ ഉപേക്ഷിക്കണമെന്ന് ഗാന്ധാരി ഭർത്താവിനോട് യാചിക്കുന്നു, എന്നാൽ ധൃതരാഷ്ട്രർ പാണ്ഡവരെ തിരികെ വിളിക്കുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 2.66; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Wed Apr 19 2006

verses.text: जनमेजय उवाच

meaning.en: Janamejaya said:

verses.text:
अनुज्ञातांस्तान्विदित्वा सरत्नधनसंचयान् ।
पाण्डवान्धार्तराष्ट्राणां कथमासीन्मनस्तदा ॥

meaning.en: When the Pandavas were sent away with their stores of jewels and wealth, how did the minds of the Dhartarashtras feel at that time?

verses.text: वैशंपायन उवाच

meaning.en: Vaishampayana said:

verses.text:
अनुज्ञातांस्तान्विदित्वा धृतराष्ट्रेण धीमता ।
राजन्दुःशासनः क्षिप्रं जगाम भ्रातरं प्रति ॥

meaning.en: Learning that the Pandavas had been sent away by the wise Dhritarashtra, Duhshasana quickly went to his brother, king.

verses.text:
दुर्योधनं समासाद्य सामात्यं भरतर्षभ ।
दुःखार्तो भरतश्रेष्ठ इदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥

meaning.en: Reaching Duryodhana with his ministers, Duhshasana, best of Bharatas, pained with grief, said this.

verses.text:
दुःखेनैतत्समानीतं स्थविरो नाशयत्यसौ ।
शत्रुसाद्गमयद्द्रव्यं तद्बुध्यध्वं महारथाः ॥

meaning.en: This wealth, gathered with such trouble, the old man is destroying; he has made it enemy property. Understand that, great warriors.

verses.text:
अथ दुर्योधनः कर्णः शकुनिश्चापि सौबलः ।
मिथः संगम्य सहिताः पाण्डवान्प्रति मानिनः ॥

meaning.en: Then Duryodhana, Karna and Shakuni, Subala's son, proud against the Pandavas, met together.

verses.text:
वैचित्रवीर्यं राजानं धृतराष्ट्रं मनीषिणम् ।
अभिगम्य त्वरायुक्ताः श्लक्ष्णं वचनमब्रुवन् ॥

meaning.en: Hurrying to the wise king Dhritarashtra, Vichitravirya's son, they spoke soft words.

verses.text: दुर्योधन उवाच

meaning.en: Duryodhana said:

verses.text:
न त्वयेदं श्रुतं राजन्यज्जगाद बृहस्पतिः ।
शक्रस्य नीतिं प्रवदन्विद्वान्देवपुरोहितः ॥

meaning.en: King, you have not heard what Brihaspati, the learned priest of the gods, said when he taught Indra's policy.

verses.text:
सर्वोपायैर्निहन्तव्याः शत्रवः शत्रुकर्षण ।
पुरा युद्धाद्बलाद्वापि प्रकुर्वन्ति तवाहितम् ॥

meaning.en: Enemies, tormentor of foes, must be killed by every means, since they will do you harm, whether before a war or by force.

verses.text:
ते वयं पाण्डवधनैः सर्वान्संपूज्य पार्थिवान् ।
यदि तान्योधयिष्यामः किं वा नः परिहास्यति ॥

meaning.en: If we, after honoring all the kings with the Pandavas' wealth, were to fight them, what would we lose?

verses.text:
अहीनाशीविषान्क्रुद्धान्दंशाय समुपस्थितान् ।
कृत्वा कण्ठे च पृष्ठे च कः समुत्स्रष्टुमर्हति ॥

meaning.en: Who would loose angry poisonous snakes that have come to bite, after putting them round his neck and back?

verses.text:
आत्तशस्त्रा रथगताः कुपितास्तात पाण्डवाः ।
निःशेषं नः करिष्यन्ति क्रुद्धा ह्याशीविषा यथा ॥

meaning.en: Pandavas, enraged, armed and in chariots, will leave nothing of us, like angry vipers.

verses.text:
संनद्धो ह्यर्जुनो याति विवृत्य परमेषुधी ।
गाण्डीवं मुहुरादत्ते निःश्वसंश्च निरीक्षते ॥

meaning.en: Arjuna goes armored, with his great quivers uncovered; he takes up Gandiva again and again, sighing as he looks around.

verses.text:
गदां गुर्वीं समुद्यम्य त्वरितश्च वृकोदरः ।
स्वरथं योजयित्वाशु निर्यात इति नः श्रुतम् ॥

meaning.en: We have heard that Vrikodara, quickly raising his heavy mace, harnessed his chariot and sped off.

verses.text:
नकुलः खड्गमादाय चर्म चाप्यष्टचन्द्रकम् ।
सहदेवश्च राजा च चक्रुराकारमिङ्गितैः ॥

meaning.en: Nakula took his sword and a shield with eight moons, and Sahadeva and the king made their intent clear by signs.

verses.text:
ते त्वास्थाय रथान्सर्वे बहुशस्त्रपरिच्छदान् ।
अभिघ्नन्तो रथव्रातान्सेनायोगाय निर्ययुः ॥

meaning.en: All of them mounted chariots fitted with many weapons, striking the chariot-throngs, and set out to join an army.

verses.text:
न क्षंस्यन्ते तथास्माभिर्जातु विप्रकृता हि ते ।
द्रौपद्याश्च परिक्लेशं कस्तेषां क्षन्तुमर्हति ॥

meaning.en: They will never forgive us, for they were wronged; and who could forgive them the humiliation of Draupadi?

verses.text:
पुनर्दीव्याम भद्रं ते वनवासाय पाण्डवैः ।
एवमेतान्वशे कर्तुं शक्ष्यामो भरतर्षभ ॥

meaning.en: May you fare well; let us play again so that the Pandavas go to live in the forest. That way we can bring them under our control, bull of the Bharatas.

verses.text:
ते वा द्वादश वर्षाणि वयं वा द्यूतनिर्जिताः ।
प्रविशेम महारण्यमजिनैः प्रतिवासिताः ॥

meaning.en: Either they, defeated at dice, enter the great forest for twelve years, clothed in deerskins, or we do.

verses.text:
त्रयोदशं च सजने अज्ञाताः परिवत्सरम् ।
ज्ञाताश्च पुनरन्यानि वने वर्षाणि द्वादश ॥

meaning.en: And in the thirteenth year they must live unknown among people, and if recognized, spend another twelve years in the forest.

verses.text:
निवसेम वयं ते वा तथा द्यूतं प्रवर्तताम् ।
अक्षानुप्त्वा पुनर्द्यूतमिदं दीव्यन्तु पाण्डवाः ॥

meaning.en: Either we live so, or they; let the game proceed so. Let the Pandavas cast the dice and play again.

verses.text:
एतत्कृत्यतमं राजन्नस्माकं भरतर्षभ ।
अयं हि शकुनिर्वेद सविद्यामक्षसंपदम् ॥

meaning.en: This is the most necessary thing for us, king. Shakuni knows the lore of dice, the wealth of the game.

verses.text:
दृढमूला वयं राज्ये मित्राणि परिगृह्य च ।
सारवद्विपुलं सैन्यं सत्कृत्य च दुरासदम् ॥

meaning.en: We are firmly rooted in the kingdom, having won friends and having a vast, strong army, honored and hard to attack.

verses.text:
ते च त्रयोदशे वर्षे पारयिष्यन्ति चेद्व्रतम् ।
जेष्यामस्तान्वयं राजन्रोचतां ते परंतप ॥

meaning.en: If they complete the vow in the thirteenth year, we will conquer them; let this please you, scorcher of foes.

verses.text: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच

meaning.en: Dhritarashtra said:

verses.text:
तूर्णं प्रत्यानयस्वैतान्कामं व्यध्वगतानपि ।
आगच्छन्तु पुनर्द्यूतमिदं कुर्वन्तु पाण्डवाः ॥

meaning.en: Quickly bring them back, even if they have gone far on the road. Let the Pandavas come and play this dice game again.

verses.text: वैशंपायन उवाच

meaning.en: Vaishampayana said:

verses.text:
ततो द्रोणः सोमदत्तो बाह्लीकश्च महारथः ।
विदुरो द्रोणपुत्रश्च वैश्यापुत्रश्च वीर्यवान् ॥

meaning.en: Then Drona, Somadatta, the great warrior Bahlika, Vidura, Drona's son, the mighty Vaishya's son Yuyutsu,

verses.text:
भूरिश्रवाः शांतनवो विकर्णश्च महारथः ।
मा द्यूतमित्यभाषन्त शमोऽस्त्विति च सर्वशः ॥

meaning.en: Bhurishravas, Bhishma Shantanava and the great warrior Vikarna said, No gambling; let there be peace, all of them.

verses.text:
अकामानां च सर्वेषां सुहृदामर्थदर्शिनाम् ।
अकरोत्पाण्डवाह्वानं धृतराष्ट्रः सुतप्रियः ॥

meaning.en: Though all his well-wishers who saw the good were unwilling, Dhritarashtra, fond of his son, ordered the Pandavas called.

verses.text:
अथाब्रवीन्महाराज धृतराष्ट्रं जनेश्वरम् ।
पुत्रहार्दाद्धर्मयुक्तं गान्धारी शोककर्शिता ॥

meaning.en: Then Gandhari, wasted with grief, spoke to King Dhritarashtra, out of love for her sons, in words full of dharma.

verses.text:
जाते दुर्योधने क्षत्ता महामतिरभाषत ।
नीयतां परलोकाय साध्वयं कुलपांसनः ॥

meaning.en: When Duryodhana was born, the wise Vidura said, Let this disgrace of the family be taken away to the next world.

verses.text:
व्यनदज्जातमात्रो हि गोमायुरिव भारत ।
अन्तो नूनं कुलस्यास्य कुरवस्तन्निबोधत ॥

meaning.en: For as soon as he was born he howled like a jackal, Bharata. This will surely be the end of this family; Kurus, understand.

verses.text:
मा बालानामशिष्टानामभिमंस्था मतिं प्रभो ।
मा कुलस्य क्षये घोरे कारणं त्वं भविष्यसि ॥

meaning.en: Lord, do not accept the counsel of ill-taught children. Do not become the cause of the terrible destruction of the family.

verses.text:
बद्धं सेतुं को नु भिन्द्याद्धमेच्छान्तं च पावकम् ।
शमे धृतान्पुनः पार्थान्कोपयेत्को नु भारत ॥

meaning.en: Who would break a built dam, or rekindle a quenched fire? Who would anger the Parthas again, who stand in peace?

verses.text:
स्मरन्तं त्वामाजमीढ स्मारयिष्याम्यहं पुनः ।
शास्त्रं न शास्ति दुर्बुद्धिं श्रेयसे वेतराय वा ॥

meaning.en: Descendant of Ajamidha, I will remind you of what you remember. Scripture does not instruct one of bad mind, whether for good or otherwise.

verses.text:
न वै वृद्धो बालमतिर्भवेद्राजन्कथंचन ।
त्वन्नेत्राः सन्तु ते पुत्रा मा त्वां दीर्णाः प्रहासिषुः ॥

meaning.en: A man grown old should never be childish-minded, king. Let your sons be led by you; do not let them, split apart, abandon you.

verses.text:
शमेन धर्मेण परस्य बुद्ध्या
जाता बुद्धिः सास्तु ते मा प्रतीपा ।
प्रध्वंसिनी क्रूरसमाहिता श्री-
र्मृदुप्रौढा गच्छति पुत्रपौत्रान् ॥

meaning.en: Let the understanding that came to you through peace, dharma and the thinking of others not turn against you. Wealth gathered by cruelty destroys; that held with gentleness and firmness passes to sons and grandsons.

verses.text:
अथाब्रवीन्महाराजो गान्धारीं धर्मदर्शिनीम् ।
अन्तः कामं कुलस्यास्तु न शक्ष्यामि निवारितुम् ॥

meaning.en: Then the great king said to Gandhari, who saw dharma: Let the family's end come as it will; I cannot prevent it.

verses.text:
यथेच्छन्ति तथैवास्तु प्रत्यागच्छन्तु पाण्डवाः ।
पुनर्द्यूतं प्रकुर्वन्तु मामकाः पाण्डवैः सह ॥

meaning.en: Let it be as they wish; let the Pandavas come back; let my sons play dice again with the Pandavas.
